question.text: In a meter Bridge experiment resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is connected in the right gap. When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> are connected in the left gap separately the balance points are <math><mn>40</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math><mn>50</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> respectively from the left end. Now if both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>&</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> are connected in series in the left gap with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> in the right gap then what will be the new balance point from the left end (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>)?
